items.claim: Aliased object leaf: its fields are marked under the alias's key, but drawn under the target's path (A+B: A's 1st finding, B's 4th)
`panelSource` keeps one leaf per path, so `stateAt` and the reset gate answer for the wrong leaf (A+B: A's 2nd, B's 2nd)
`sharedRows` pairs an object's fields across sections and inside bars, where `ObjectLeaf` draws them apart (A+B: A's 3rd, B's 3rd)
Top-level leaves pair across the sections between them; nested ones don't
items.note: `flatten` deliberately draws every top-level leaf together in the leading untitled section. So a and b are neighbors as drawn, and the pair and its marks match what is on screen.

items.claim: An object leaf's action field never draws pressed in a selection panel, because `leafContext` hands no `activeAt`
items.note: This also adds `activeAt` to `PrefAliasTargets` in prefs (a minor changeset), so an alias into an `over` schema answers too.

items.claim: Across several kinds, every node is read, clamped, and reset under the first kind's leaf
items.note: This needed a behavior call nobody had made, so I made the strict one: a leaf is shared across kinds only where every kind's leaf differs at most in how it is drawn. It is recorded in `docs/unruled.md` under "Audit round fifty-nine". None of core's built-in kinds differ this way, so a mixed selection of them keeps every leaf it had.

items.claim: A glyph-named flag toggle in a paired object row takes an even share of the row
items.note: (CSS only). It has no test, because only a browser layout test could catch it and none can run here.
